“It sounds much better. It is much better and it’s much more accurate.”
He said the name change was necessary because the word “artificial” makes it “sound fake.”
Trump said, saying that referring to the technology as “artificial” is misleading.
Trump dismissed fears about [artificial intelligence](https://www.washingtontimes.com/topics/artificial-intelligence/) as a “hoax,” brushing aside warnings from tech experts that the technology is growing faster than tech companies understand.

item.title: The State of Illinois Newsroom
item.description:
# **Gov. Pritzker Establishes Illinois Artificial Intelligence (AI) Cabinet** [![](https://cdn.uc.assets.prezly.com/ed4be510-b1ca-473b-8835-fa093fe95ae2/-/crop/2100x1045/0,88/-/preview/-/format/auto/Prezly%20Header.png)](https://cdn.uc.assets.prezly.com/ed4be510-b1ca-473b-8835-fa093fe95ae2/-/crop/2100x1045/0,88/-/preview/Prezly%20Header.png) **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:** September 22, 2026 ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ **CONTACT:** [Gov.Press@illinois.gov](mailto:Gov.Press@illinois.gov) ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​
**CHICAGO** – Governor JB Pritzker today signed [Executive Order 2026-07](https://www.illinois.gov/government/executive-orders/executive-order.executive-order-2026-07.2026.html) establishing the Illinois Artificial Intelligence (AI) Cabinet, a group of individuals from across industries and fields that will assess the various risks posed by AI to the safety of Illinoisans. As AI continues to rapidly advance, the Illinois AI Cabinet will advise state government on preparing for and responding to AI-related incidents, identifying safeguards for public assets and infrastructure, and evaluating additional steps Illinois can take to strengthen AI safety and accountability. The AI cabinet will include a broad cross-sector of experts from academia, law, ethics, governance and more. ​
“Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” **said Governor JB Pritzker.**
"Governor Pritzker's formation of an AI Cabinet will bring together experts from several of our state agencies to assess the risks of artificial intelligence and regulating it accordingly," **said Lieutenant Governor Juliana Stratton**. Together, we’ll find new ways to innovate while protecting our people at every turn."
“We are eager to help the state navigate the current challenges and opportunities that AI brings,” **said University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Chancellor Charles Isbell.** “As a land-grant institution, we are the committed to innovation for the public good and to developing human-centered AI that protects privacy, reduces bias, strengthens democratic institutions, uses energy wisely, and creates value for workers, companies and communities.
Governor Pritzker is again taking proactive steps after signing nation-leading AI regulations into law this summer, the [**Artificial Intelligence (AI) Safety Measures Act**](https://gov-pritzker-newsroom.prezly.com/gov-pritzker-signs-nation-leading-artificial-intelligence-safety-law) creates a framework placed for AI safety, accountability, and transparency. This framework implemented risk identification, disclosure, and mitigation requirements on the largest AI developers in the state, including making Illinois the first state to require annual independent third-party audits, and amongst the first to provide protections for workers who report safety concerns – an essential safeguard as safety concerns rise in the very development hubs where AI continues to evolve**. **
- Provide cross‑sector expertise to develop comprehensive recommendations on AI safety, risk management, and regulation. - Make timely policy recommendations to Illinois state agencies and government bodies based on current information about AI risks and best practices.
- Develop policies and procedures to prepare for, prevent, and respond to AI‑related incidents that may impact the safety of Illinois residents. - Analyze emerging AI incidents and share lessons learned to strengthen statewide preparedness and response.
- Create policies and procedures to safeguard public assets—including public buildings, water systems, education systems, and information infrastructure—from AI‑driven threats.
The AI Cabinet will bring together academic and subject-matter experts alongside senior leaders from the [Department of Innovation and Technology (DoIT),](https://doit.illinois.gov/) the [Illinois Emergency Management Agency (IEMA)](https://iemaohs.illinois.gov/), the [Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR)](https://idfpr.illinois.gov/), the [Illinois Commerce Commission (ICC)](https://www.illinois.gov/agencies/agency.icc.html), the [Illinois State Police (ISP)](https://isp.illinois.gov/), the [Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO)](https://dceo.illinois.gov/), the Illinois [Environmental Protection Agency (IEPA),](https://epa.illinois.gov/) and the [Illinois Department of Public Health](http://www.idph.state.il.us/), which are state agencies responsible for technology, emergency management, financial regulation, utilities, public safety, economic development, and environmental protection.
